headline: Preprint reports better test-time scaling from parallel teams of agents
summary: A Nov 6 preprint studies verifier-scored long-horizon tasks using Qwen3.8-27B agents in the Codex harness. The authors report that, at a budget of 100 agents, the best of ten collaborating teams of ten scores higher than the best of 100 independent agents on 10 of 12 tasks, and higher than one team of 100 on all four tasks tested at that size. Averaged across 12 tasks, the paper reports 10% higher scores at a 10-agent budget and 27% at 100 agents. The method combines within-team information sharing through a flat shared forum with best-of-N selection across independent teams. These are author-reported results: large-team runs have only one to five trials per size, the study uses one model family and one harness, and the linked code repository currently returns 404. Independent replication and transfer remain unestablished.
